# All corrected odd-open and even-closed XOR-magic degrees at powers of two

DRAFT - 1 November 2026 (America/Los_Angeles). Prepared with AI assistance by the Codex research agent. No human authorship or affiliation is asserted. This is an unaccepted research draft; accepted credit is zero and the campaign count remains 14/20 beyond 39.

## Abstract

For every n >= 4, we construct a connected simple open zero-XOR graph of order 2^n for each odd degree from 5 through 2^n-5, and a connected simple closed zero-XOR graph for each even degree from 4 through 2^n-6. A four-fold affine lift over F4 preserves low-degree seeds and their matching decompositions; block replacement then supplies all intermediate degrees. Complements give the top degrees. Finite certificates supply orders 16 and 32. The complete existence theorem is formalized in Lean, together with the uniform negation of the printed Conjecture 25 of Cichacz, Grochowski and Zuazua [1]. Its printed closed endpoint 2^n-4 is already forbidden by their Proposition 24, attributed to Batal. That correction carries no novelty claim. The dossier contains source-identical Lean modules from xor-magic-formal-r5, a portable strict replay, declaration audits and negative controls.

## 1. Source statement and corrected theorem

Write N=2^n and A_n=(Z/2Z)^n. A graph is simple and connected. An open XOR-magic labeling is a bijection l:V -> A_n for which sum_{u in N(v)} l(u)=0 at every vertex. A closed XOR-magic labeling instead requires l(v)+sum_{u in N(v)} l(u)=0. The constant must be zero; an arbitrary group-distance-magic constant is insufficient. Degree d means regularity at every vertex. The order follows from bijectivity.

Conjecture 25 [1, Section 4] asserts existence for each d in {5,7,...,2^n-7,2^n-5} in the open case and each d in {4,6,...,2^n-6,2^n-4} in the closed case. It leaves n implicit. In the nonempty intended scope n >= 4, its fully quantified interpretation is: for every n >= 4, every odd integer d with 5 <= d <= 2^n-5 has an open witness, and every even integer d with 4 <= d <= 2^n-4 has a closed witness. MathDB 372205 says n is positive; that universal reading is also false, since n=4 already refutes it.

Theorem 1 (corrected complete existence). For every integer n >= 4, open witnesses exist for every odd 5 <= d <= 2^n-5, and closed witnesses exist for every even 4 <= d <= 2^n-6. Together with Proposition 24 of [1], these are precisely the possible degrees within the odd-open and even-closed parity classes. This does not classify graphs or address arbitrary labeling groups.

Theorem 2 (printed obstruction). For every n >= 4 the printed assertion is false. This is a zero-credit correction of an inconsistency already excluded by Proposition 24, not an independent discovery. Sections 2-6 prove Theorem 1; Section 2 also proves Theorem 2.
<!-- PAGE -->
## 2. Complements and the affine lift

For n >= 2, the sum of every element of A_n is zero: each coordinate is 1 exactly 2^(n-1) times, an even number. Partitioning V into {v}, N_G(v), and N_complement(v) gives

    sum_{u in N_complement(v)} l(u)
      = l(v) + sum_{u in N_G(v)} l(u).                    (1)

Thus complementation swaps the two zero-sum conditions, irrespective of connectivity. To obtain XOR-magic graphs in the source's sense one must establish connectivity separately. If a graph on N vertices has minimum degree at least N/2, every component has at least N/2+1 vertices, so it is connected.

Suppose a closed (N-4)-regular witness exists. Its complement is cubic and open-zero by (1). Let z have label 0 and let u be a neighbor of z. The other two neighbors a,b of u are distinct and satisfy l(a)+l(b)=0. In characteristic two l(a)=l(b), contrary to injectivity. This does not need connectivity. It is the closed N-4 obstruction already credited to Batal in [1, Proposition 24].

For completeness, open degree 1 would force all neighbors to have label zero. Open degree 3 is excluded by the preceding argument. Degree N-1 has open sum l(v), not identically zero. At degree N-3, the two vertices outside each closed neighborhood must have label sum l(v); at z labeled zero they would have equal labels. These exclude all four odd degrees outside Theorem 1. Identity (1) transfers the four exclusions to closed degrees 0,2,N-4,N-2. These necessity arguments are ordinary mathematics here; the advertised Lean endpoints certify the corrected positive ranges and the printed N-4 obstruction.

A seed consists of a connected d-regular zero-XOR graph G on m=2^r vertices, of the required type, with d >= 4, ordered perfect-matching decompositions M_0,...,M_(d-1) of G and of its complement, and a proper Boolean coloring of M_0 union M_1. It also carries an oriented genuine cycle C in that union, of length L >= 3 with 3 not dividing L. The orientation specified below must follow C consistently.

Use F4={0,1,w,w^2}, w^2+w+1=0. Direct M_0 from color true to false and M_1 from false to true. At every vertex exactly one of these edges enters and one leaves, so every cycle is oriented consistently. Give a directed cycle edge slope w and its reverse w^-1; all other edges have slope 1. Choose one orientation of each undirected edge for indexing. Let a_e denote its slope, and put T_e(x)=a_e x+c_e. The reverse is a_e^-1 x+a_e^-1 c_e. Define the lift on V x F4 by joining (u,x) to (v,T_e(x)) for e=(u,v). It is simple, d-regular, and labeled bijectively by (l(u),x) in A_(r+2).

Two perfect matchings have even cycle lengths and hence admit a proper coloring. The seed includes a chosen coloring to make the orientation and its persistence literal, rather than relying on an unspecified later choice.
<!-- PAGE -->
## 3. Choosing the translations and proving connectivity

Define additive (indeed F4-linear) maps D:F4^V -> F4^E and B:F4^E -> F4^V by

    (Db)_e = b_v + a_e b_u,        e=(u,v),
    column_e(B): 1 at u, a_e^-1 at v, zero elsewhere.     (2)

Here Bc is exactly the vector of constant terms in the lifted neighborhood sums. We need c in ker B but outside im D. The following cardinality argument is the one used in Lean, and requires no rank assertion about either map.

Since |E|=dm/2 >= 2m, |F4^E| >= |F4^V|^2. The composite BD is nonzero: for adjacent distinct u,v its (u,v) coefficient is 1, since their unique edge contributes 1 and no other edge contributes to that off-diagonal entry. Thus im D is not contained in ker B. If ker B were contained in im D, this would be a proper inclusion, so

    |ker B| < |im D| <= |F4^V|.

But |F4^E|=|ker B| |im B| and |im B| <= |F4^V|, contradicting the previous lower bound. Choose c in ker B outside im D. Finite enumeration could make the choice effective; no random success assumption is used.

At (u,x) the first label coordinate is the base zero-sum condition, with l(u) added for the closed case. Put epsilon=0 for open and 1 for closed. The second-coordinate linear coefficient is

    (d-2) + w + w^-1 + epsilon = d+1+epsilon = 0,        (3)

because w+w^-1=1, and d is odd in the open case or even in the closed case. The constant term is (Bc)_u=0. Therefore the lift is zero-XOR of the same type.

We now prove connectivity directly by fibre sizes, avoiding an unproved holonomy-transitivity equivalence. Fix a lifted component K and let S_u={x:(u,x) in K}. Every edge bijection T_uv sends S_u onto S_v: an edge gives one inclusion and its inverse gives the other. Connectivity of G implies that all these sets have the same positive cardinality t.

Around C the composite affine map is x -> a x+b with a=w^L != 1. Such a map has exactly one fixed point (solve (1+a)x=b); conjugating by that point identifies it with multiplication by a, whose remaining orbit has length 3. The set S at the starting vertex is invariant under this map and its inverse. Therefore t is 0,1,3, or 4, never 2. Positivity rules out 0.

If t=1, the unique b_u in S_u obeys T_uv(b_u)=b_v. If t=3, the unique b_u outside S_u obeys the same identity because each edge map also transports complements. Either case gives c_e=b_v+a_e b_u, that is, c=Db, a contradiction. Hence t=4 for every component and every base vertex. Each component therefore contains all vertices of every fibre, proving that the lift is connected. This supplies the precise argument missing in the earlier ordinary exposition.
<!-- PAGE -->
## 4. Persistence and interpolation

Each base perfect matching lifts to a perfect matching: every vertex has exactly one partner over its base mate, with inverse partner map. These lifted matchings partition the lifted graph. Its complement also factors into perfect matchings. Inside each fibre, decompose K4 into its three translation matchings x <-> x+t, t != 0. Over a base G matching the missing edges form K4,4 minus the designated matching; the three maps x -> T_e(x)+t, t != 0, split it into three matchings. Over a base-complement matching, the four maps x -> x+t split the full K4,4. The resulting number is

    3 + 3d + 4(m-1-d) = 4m-1-d.

Every complement edge lies in exactly one of these disjoint blocks. The global base matchings ensure these blockwise matchings cover every lifted vertex exactly once.

Color (u,x) by the color of u. This remains proper on the first two lifted factors. The affine return map around C has a fixed point x_0 by Section 3. Starting there and lifting C gives a closed walk of length L. It is a genuine simple cycle: its projected vertices before return are distinct. It uses the first two lifted factors, keeps their orientation and the same sequence of base colors, and still has 3 not dividing L. Its other return orbit yields a cycle of length 3L, but only the fixed-point cycle is needed. Thus the entire colored seed structure persists. Repeated lifts give degree-4 closed and degree-5 open seeds with both factor decompositions at each exponent r+2.

For interpolation, begin with a lift of a degree-d seed on m vertices. Choose k entire factors of G, 0 <= k <= d. Over their edges replace the designated matching by its three-edge complement in K4,4, increasing every degree by 2k. Choose j entire factors of the base complement, 0 <= j <= m-1-d, and add their full K4,4 blocks, increasing every degree by 4j. Hence the new degree is

    q = d + 2k + 4j.                                    (4)

The sum of all four labels in any fibre is zero: the first coordinate occurs four times and the sum of F4 is zero. A matching edge and the complementary three edges consequently give the same label sum at their endpoint; a full block contributes zero. Thus all neighborhood zero sums persist, including the vertex term in the closed case.

Connectivity needs two cases. If k=0, the original connected lift remains a subgraph. If k>0, one replaced block is K4,4 minus a matching, which is connected: any two vertices on one side share at least two neighbors, and every vertex has a neighbor on the other side. All four vertices in its endpoint fibres are therefore in one component. Along every adjacent base edge, either a matching or a triple block meets every vertex in the next fibre. This propagates fullness through connected G. Added full blocks do not destroy paths.

Dividing q-d by 2, the possible increments form the integer intervals [2j,2j+d], for 0 <= j <= m-1-d. Consecutive intervals overlap since d >= 4. Their union is [0,2m-2-d], so all degrees of parity d from d to 4m-4-d occur.
<!-- PAGE -->
## 5. Finite bases and their certificates

Vertices at order 2^r are integers 0,...,2^r-1 with their binary labels (least significant bit is coordinate 0). Encode row v of the adjacency matrix by the hexadecimal integer h_v, where bit u is 1 exactly when u is adjacent to v. The four persistent seeds have the following compact data. The row arrays, all remaining base witnesses, descent parents and ranks are also in base-data.json; the Lean sources contain the literal lists.

    Base16Open5:

A row list proves the finite conditions by checking symmetry, zero diagonal, exactly d set bits in each row, and XOR of the set-bit indices equal to 0 (open) or v (closed). Connectivity has a separate certificate: parents p(v) and natural ranks r(v), with v adjacent to p(v) and r(p(v)) < r(v) for every v != 0. Iterating parents terminates at 0, yielding a path from every vertex. These checks use only finite integer arithmetic, not a solver's feasibility verdict. The supplied certify_bases.py independently checks every row and every descent, while the corresponding Base*.lean modules prove them by kernel reduction.

At order 16, open degrees 5,7,9,11 and closed degrees 4,6,8,10 have direct certificates. At order 32, open degrees 5,7,...,27 and closed degrees 4,6,...,26 have direct certificates. In particular Base16Closed6 and Base32Closed4 each have their own parents, ranks and descent theorem. These are the two low-degree complements for which the minimum-degree bound does not apply. Their connectivity is certified directly; no invocation of a high-degree complement lemma is made.

For seed iteration the ordered matching lists live in Seed16Closed4, Seed16Open5, Seed32Closed4 and Seed32Open5. Their mate arrays are involutions without fixed points; distinct factor mates at each vertex and coverage of adjacency prove a decomposition. Complement factors satisfy the same conditions. ColourSeed* supplies the Boolean color lists and an indexed oriented walk with an IsCycle proof. The distinguished cycle lengths are 16,16,32,8 respectively. Every one is at least 3 and not divisible by 3. The union for the order-32 open seed has cycles of lengths 8,16,8; the chosen cycle has length 8.

The original authors' graph files at immutable repository revision 7f21f7e0ade3f35b95c1593af97af5defcd54f02 supply several base examples, including the open order-32 degree-27 graph whose complement is the closed degree-4 seed. The dossier preserves those files as inert text. The local closed degree-6 witness at order 32 and other local finite witnesses supplement these bases. Base discovery by an optimizer is separate from exact verification of its edge data.
<!-- PAGE -->
## 6. Induction and the final ranges

Starting separately with exponent 4 and exponent 5, Sections 2-4 produce both colored low-degree seeds at every exponent n >= 4 by steps of two. Relabeling V x F4 by Fin (4m) transports adjacency, labels, mate arrays, coloring, and the actual indexed distinguished cycle. The walk itself is retained, so no claim that an arbitrary closed walk is a cycle enters the induction.

Now let n >= 6 and put N=2^n and m=2^(n-2). There are degree-5 open and degree-4 closed seeds on m vertices. Formula (4) applied to them supplies respectively

    open odd degrees:     5,7,...,N-9;
    closed even degrees:  4,6,...,N-8.                   (5)

Closed degrees 4 and 6 are included in (5). Their complements have open degrees N-5 and N-7. Open degree 5 is included in (5); its complement has closed degree N-6. Since N >= 64, all three complementary degrees are at least N/2. Their complements are therefore connected by the component-size bound of Section 2. Equation (1) proves their required zero sums. Combining these endpoints with (5) proves exactly the two ranges in Theorem 1. For n=4 and n=5 use Section 5's direct certificates, completing both induction parities.

The proof does not append closed degree N-4: Section 2 proves it impossible. Proposition 24's exclusions together with the construction give the complete existence picture only for odd-open and even-closed degrees, as specified. No restriction to bipartite, Cayley, vertex-transitive or planar graphs is asserted. The coloring concerns two matching factors, not the whole graph.

## 7. Literal formal statement

The Lean dossier uses the following definitions verbatim from Literal.lean. The context is V : Type with Fintype V and DecidableEq V; each graph has a decidable adjacency relation. Natural subtraction is harmless in the advertised n >= 4 range. A simple graph is part of the type, connectedness is explicit, and the equivalence supplies every label exactly once.

    abbrev Bits (n : Nat) := Fin n -> ZMod 2

The six literal definitions are displayed on the next page using the original Lean notation. Their type quantifiers prevent the existential graph from being fixed in advance: the witness may depend on n and on the requested degree d. The finite underlying type is allowed to vary. No construction hypothesis, unproved seed premise, or assumed connectivity remains in the final endpoints.

The main theorem is XorMagic.corrected_all : forall n : Nat, 4 <= n -> CorrectedAt n. The second endpoint is XorMagic.not_printed_each_ge_four : forall n : Nat, 4 <= n -> not (PrintedAt n). The latter is a pointwise impossibility assertion at every exponent in scope, stronger than merely finding one failure of the universal printed claim. The re-exports printed_not_all and printed_not_positive also negate the unrestricted and positive-exponent readings. These statements have different scientific roles: only the corrected existence theorem supplies the substantive construction.
<!-- PAGE -->
## 7. Literal definitions (continued)

    def OpenMagic (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (n : ℕ) : Prop :=

      G.Connected ∧ ∃ l : V ≃ Bits n, ∀ v, ∑ u ∈ G.neighborFinset v, l u = 0

    

    def ClosedMagic (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (n : ℕ) : Prop :=

      G.Connected ∧ ∃ l : V ≃ Bits n, ∀ v, l v + ∑ u ∈ G.neighborFinset v, l u = 0

    

    def OpenExists (n d : ℕ) : Prop :=

      ∃ (V : Type) (_ : Fintype V) (_ : DecidableEq V) (G : SimpleGraph V)

        (_ : DecidableRel G.Adj), G.IsRegularOfDegree d ∧ OpenMagic G n

    

    def ClosedExists (n d : ℕ) : Prop :=

      ∃ (V : Type) (_ : Fintype V) (_ : DecidableEq V) (G : SimpleGraph V)

        (_ : DecidableRel G.Adj), G.IsRegularOfDegree d ∧ ClosedMagic G n

    

    def PrintedAt (n : ℕ) : Prop :=

      (∀ d, Odd d → 5 ≤ d → d ≤ 2^n-5 → OpenExists n d) ∧

      (∀ d, Even d → 4 ≤ d → d ≤ 2^n-4 → ClosedExists n d)

    

    def CorrectedAt (n : ℕ) : Prop :=

      (∀ d, Odd d → 5 ≤ d → d ≤ 2^n-5 → OpenExists n d) ∧

      (∀ d, Even d → 4 ≤ d → d ≤ 2^n-6 → ClosedExists n d)

The namespace of these definitions is XorMagic. The declarations appear without alterations in the source-only packet; all 107 Lean modules are byte-identical to xor-magic-formal-r5/formal. The prose expansion on the previous page explains the binders but does not replace the literal source.

In particular OpenMagic and ClosedMagic conjoin connectedness with existence of a bijective zero-sum labeling. OpenExists and ClosedExists additionally quantify the simple graph and demand degree regularity. PrintedAt includes the forbidden closed upper bound; CorrectedAt changes that bound to 2^n-6 and preserves the entire open range. Finite decidability instances are elaboration data and do not weaken these propositions.
<!-- PAGE -->
## 8. Correspondence, replay, and trust

Only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound are allowed as transitive axioms. The packet's audits inspect local declarations, full types and bodies, safety flags and transitive axioms, including auxiliary declarations. Shared expression DAGs are checked independently; duplicate generated declarations must have identical canonical type and body hashes. No sorry, admit, new axioms, unsafe, native_decide or ofReduceBool is permitted in the delivered proof modules. The audit does not reinterpret upstream mathlib theorems.

The pinned installation is Lean 4.34.1, commit 5045d0056413266e57c625dcd7c365b10e377c52. The read-only package cache uses mathlib d13f23b723b8a846827a245b89c10fc7d3f11612. Set LEAN_BIN and LEAN_PACKAGES as documented in REPRODUCE.md. The portable driver rejects existing oleans, checks source hashes, discards inherited Lean configuration, retains actual HOME, and writes logs and per-call receipts. Each module is compiled with -j1 -DwarningAsError=true, then checked by leanchecker. The extraction is fresh and path-safe. All deletions, if any, are confined to driver-owned temporary files; this version requires no cleanup deletions.

Each child invocation has affinity to at most two CPUs, 120 CPU seconds, a 140-second wall guard, aggregate sampled RSS <= 6 GiB and MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2. Upstream cached oleans are trusted. leanchecker shares the same installation; it is an additional check, not an independent implementation of Lean's kernel. Sampling RSS is not a continuous hardware-enforced memory measurement.

Negative controls deliberately corrupt concrete arithmetic, labels, sums, degrees, seed and coloring facts, slope/reverse/composition facts, incidence and holonomy facts, the top endpoint and the inference from CorrectedAt to PrintedAt. Their rejection demonstrates only rejection of these particular false claims with imports resolved; it does not prove the completeness of the audit or guard against every possible specification error. The source-only archive contains no oleans. The full dossier adds the manuscript, evidence, QA images, receipts and manifests. Replay results and hashes are recorded outside this static draft in results.json and SUMMARY.md. Root must perform the final replay and paper review before any acceptance.
<!-- PAGE -->
## 9. Related work, access limits, and bibliography

Siehler [2] develops the closed XOR condition, constructs cubic examples at every exponent at least 2, and studies small cubic graphs with nullity and row-distinctness tests. That is the odd-closed parity class, rather than the two classes constructed here. The author-copy body was read. Cichacz, Grochowski and Zuazua [1] place XOR magic within group distance magic labeling: the group is elementary abelian and the magic constant is zero. Their Theorem 5 supplies some odd-open and even-closed graph at every exponent greater than 3; their finite examples, Cartesian products and complements do not by themselves assert every degree.

Batal's construction paper is credited by [1] for both Observation 1 (complementation) and Proposition 24 (nonexistence). Those are prior results; neither the complement identity nor the printed endpoint correction is offered as novel. The body of Batal's Discrete Applied Mathematics article remains unread: the preserved publisher route returned 403, and repository access produced a bot challenge. No challenge was bypassed. The bibliographic information below for that article is explicitly indirect, from [1] and preserved metadata. Its unread body precludes a complete subsumption assessment.

Batal's arXiv:2609.05934 [3] treats generating and affinely generating group-magic maps and distance-magic labelings via modular kernels and reduced Smith groups. Its introduction explicitly relates Siehler's and Batal's XOR row-separation characterizations to this broader framework. The preserved abstract, introduction, principal statements and relevant binary discussion were read; this is a bounded screen, not a complete audit of every proof. Its order-27 example concerns a different distance-magic conjecture and does not supply the construction proved here.

The dossier inherits dated access receipts from the focused and independent-review lanes (2 November 2026 UTC / 1 November Los Angeles). No new live literature or registry search was performed for this manuscript. Empty citation lists and registry HEAD identities do not establish absence of prior proofs. The bibliography includes only primary bodies actually read, plus the explicitly marked unread Batal item required to give proper credit. No priority claim or worldwide novelty clearance is made. Independent review qualified scope and significance and passed the ordinary mathematics with the two exposition issues repaired above. Root alone can accept; credit remains zero.

[1] S. Cichacz, H. Grochowski and R. Zuazua. Open XOR-magic odd graphs and closed XOR-magic even graphs. arXiv:2512.19278v1, 22 December 2025. https://arxiv.org/html/2512.19278v1. Definitions; Observation 1; Theorems 5, 17, 18; Corollary 20; Proposition 24; Conjecture 25. Primary body read. Associated graph data: grochowskih/RegularXorMagicGraphs, revision 7f21f7e0ade3f35b95c1593af97af5defcd54f02.

[2] J. A. Siehler. Xor-magic graphs. Recreational Mathematics Magazine 6(11) (2019), 35-44. DOI 10.2478/rmm-2019-0004. Primary author-copy body read, especially Theorems 1-4; preserved under evidence/xor-magic-review-r1/work/web/siehler/.

[3] A. Batal. Algebraic characterizations of generating and affinely generating Gamma-magic maps and Gamma-distance magic labelings on regular graphs. arXiv:2609.05934 (2026). https://arxiv.org/html/2609.05934. Primary body sections specified above read; preserved in focused sources/later.html and outputs/later.txt.

Indirect credit, body unread: A. Batal. On the construction of XOR-magic graphs. Discrete Applied Mathematics 379 (2026), 288-315. DOI 10.1016/j.dam.2025.08.055. Attribution follows [1, Observation 1 and Proposition 24]; this item is not presented as a primary body inspected for novelty clearance.

# Reproduce the XOR-magic draft dossier

DRAFT; accepted credit 0, root acceptance pending. Campaign remains 14/20 beyond 39.

The source-only ZIP is self-contained apart from the pinned upstream tools and packages. No network is needed for Lean replay. Extract into a new empty directory using safe_extract.py (or an equivalent path-safe extractor). The driver refuses any existing local .olean or .olean.* file. It never deletes user files; its logs/tmp/home directories are local to that extraction. Actual HOME is retained; inherited Lean options and plugin paths are discarded.

```
python3 -B safe_extract.py xor-magic-manuscript-source.zip my-fresh-replay
cd my-fresh-replay
export LEAN_BIN=/home/mj-kang/Documents/Dev/math/dlp-research/.tools/lean-4.34.1-linux/bin
export LEAN_PACKAGES=/home/mj-kang/Documents/Dev/math/openai-proof-research/frontier/campaigns/2026-10-14/formal/.lake/packages
python3 -B -I replay.py
```

LEAN_BIN may be a binary directory or the full path to lean. LEAN_PACKAGES contains mathlib and the other package directories with cached .lake/build/lib/lean trees. Lean must be version 4.34.1, commit 5045d0056413266e57c625dcd7c365b10e377c52; mathlib must be d13f23b723b8a846827a245b89c10fc7d3f11612. The adjacent project lake-manifest.json is checked for the mathlib revision; alternatively set LEAN_LAKE_MANIFEST to that manifest before starting. Binary SHA-256 pins and the original dependency manifest are in pins.json and upstream-lake-manifest.json. The cached upstream oleans are trusted and not rebuilt. leanchecker is from the same installation, not an independent kernel implementation.

All 107 local Lean modules must build with -j1 -DwarningAsError=true and pass leanchecker. The full declaration audit checks local bodies, types, safety, partial flags, and transitive axioms; only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound are allowed. The DAG consistency checker validates full expression graphs and duplicate declaration identities. The source modules must be byte-identical to r5. The per-call wrapper restricts affinity to 2 CPUs, CPU to 120 seconds, wall to 140 seconds, samples aggregate descendant RSS against 6 GiB, and sets MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2. Receipts report measured peak sampled RSS; transient peaks between samples are not continuously enforced. The minimal environment retains actual HOME, uses a pinned PATH, and packet-local TMPDIR. No upstream cache writes are requested.

Seventeen negative controls must fail after imports resolve. They test false concrete label, sum, degree, field, seed, orientation, cycle, incidence, affine, scalar and endpoint claims. BadFinalEndpoint attempts to specialize the corrected range to forbidden closed degree 12 at exponent 4; BadPrintedFromCorrected attempts the invalid printed inference. # MathDB 372205: literal obstruction and corrected constructive theorem

Status: ordinary mathematical argument and exact Python certificates only. No Lean endpoint; no acceptance or credit claimed. This file does NOT prove the literal Conjecture 25. Its closed endpoint is impossible. The constructive theorem below addresses the corrected range and requires independent review.

## Source fidelity

Primary source: Cichacz–Grochowski–Zuazua, arXiv:2512.19278v1, Sections 1, 3, 4. Live abs and v1 HTML were fetched on 2026-11-02 UTC (2026-11-01 Los Angeles). Abs lists only v1, submitted 2025-12-22. The literal definition requires a simple CONNECTED graph, a bijection to F2^n, and zero, not an arbitrary constant, neighbourhood sum.

Theorem 5 explicitly uses n > 3. Theorems 17 and 18 give bases at n = 4,5,6,7; Corollary 20 adds powers by Cartesian products and the proof of Theorem 5 inducts by n -> n+4. Those products establish existence of some degrees, not all degrees. Theorem 17 gives open degrees {5,7,9,11} at n=4, {5,7,9,11,13,15,27} at n=5, 9 at n=6 and 13 at n=7. Theorem 18 gives their closed complement degrees. Proposition 24 forbids closed degrees {0,2,2^n-4,2^n-2} and open degrees {1,3,2^n-3,2^n-1}. Order 8 has no examples of the required parity types.

Conjecture 25 does not explicitly quantify n. Its intended nonempty scope is n >= 4; interpreting its displayed sets as inequalities gives empty open sets for n <= 3, but a closed degree 4 at n=3, again contradicting Proposition 24. That endpoint ambiguity is not a discovery.

Even for n >= 4 the literal closed interval is 4,6,...,2^n-4. This includes the forbidden 2^n-4. In particular the assignment's characterization of closed {4,6,8,10} as the full displayed range at n=4 is incorrect: the displayed range also includes 12. The intended corrected upper endpoint is 2^n-6. The nearby source prose also gives an incorrect exclusion set and uses "odd degree" for an even-degree list. We do not silently repair the literal target.

## Literal nonexistence proof

For n >= 2 the XOR of all labels of F2^n is zero: each coordinate equals one exactly 2^(n-1) times, an even number. Thus for every vertex v,

    XOR(closed neighbours in G at v) = XOR(open neighbours in complement G at v).

This identity does not require the complement to be connected. Suppose G has degree 2^n-4 and a closed zero-XOR bijection. Its complement H is cubic and has an open zero-XOR bijection. Let z have label zero. Choose a neighbour u of z in H; cubic regularity guarantees one. The two other neighbours a,b of u are distinct, and their labels satisfy label(a)+label(b)=0. In F2^n this implies label(a)=label(b), contradicting injectivity. Therefore the closed degree 2^n-4 demanded in the literal conjecture is impossible for EVERY n >= 4. This is precisely an already stated obstruction in Proposition 24; it receives zero novelty credit.

## Corrected theorem (ordinary proof, not formalized)

For every n >= 4, there exist connected simple open zero-XOR graphs on F2^n of every odd degree 5 <= d <= 2^n-5, and closed zero-XOR graphs of every even degree 4 <= d <= 2^n-6.

Here is a constructive proof, including the connection argument omitted by a purely linear lift. Finite seed and factor certificates are in outputs/. The Python checker is not a Lean kernel certificate.

### Four-fold lift lemma

Let G have m vertices, be connected and d-regular with d >= 4, be open zero-XOR with odd d or closed zero-XOR with even d. Assume both G and its complement have decompositions into perfect matchings. Assume the union F of the first two matchings of G has a cycle whose length L is not divisible by 3.

Use F4 = F2[w]/(w^2+w+1). Orient each cycle of F. On each oriented edge use slope w in the forward direction and w^-1 in reverse; on other edges use slope 1. For a fixed orientation u -> v of each edge, write slope a_e and use the affine bijection x -> a_e x+c_e between its fibres. Reversing gives a_e^-1 x+a_e^-1 c_e.

Let D:F4^m -> F4^E send a vertex vector b to (b_v+a_e b_u)_e. Let B:F4^E -> F4^m have column e=(u,v) equal to 1 at u and a_e^-1 at v. The constant term in the neighbour-label sum is exactly Bc. We select c in ker B but outside im D.

Such c always exists. The kernel of D is zero: transporting b around the distinguished cycle multiplies it by w^L != 1, hence b=0 there and then everywhere by connectivity. The left kernel of B satisfies the identical edge relation y_v=a_e y_u, so B has rank m. Therefore dim ker B=|E|-m=(d/2-1)m >= m. On the other hand BD is a nonzero matrix, since its (u,v) entry for any edge uv is a nonzero unit and no second edge can cancel that entry in a simple graph. As D is injective, dim(im D intersect ker B)=dim ker(BD) <= m-1. Hence ker B is not contained in im D. Explicitly compute a nullspace basis and take the first basis vector outside im D. Membership in im D can be tested by propagation for the four possible values at a root. This deterministic algorithm is implemented in scripts/lift.py.

The lift has vertices (u,x) with labels (label(u),x), giving a bijection to F2^(n+2). Its degree is d and it is simple because edges only join distinct base fibres using bijections. Its first neighbourhood coordinate is the original G sum (with the vertex added in the closed case). At each vertex of F the two twisted neighbour maps contribute slopes w and w^-1, with d-2 other identity slopes. Writing epsilon=0 for open and 1 for closed, the second coordinate has linear coefficient

    (d-2) + w + w^-1 + epsilon = d + 1 + epsilon = 0 in F4,

using w+w^-1=1 and the required parity. The constant coefficient is Bc=0.

Connectivity: the holonomy group at a base vertex is a subgroup H of the affine group of F4, with scalar parts in {1,w,w^2}. Its scalar image is nontrivial, because the distinguished cycle has scalar w^L. If H contains a nonzero translation t, conjugating by an element with scalar w or w^2 gives another translation independent of t over F2; these translations act transitively on F4. If H contains no nonzero translation, its scalar map is injective, so it is cyclic of order 3 and fixes a common point. Transporting that point to every base vertex gives a section b with c=Db, contradicting our choice. Consequently H is transitive; every fibre is reachable from every other because G is connected, so the lift is connected.

Every base perfect matching lifts to a perfect matching, so G's decomposition persists. The complement also decomposes into perfect matchings. Split its internal K4 in each fibre into three matchings. Over each base G matching, split the K4,4 minus its designated matching into three matchings, using nonzero translations of its output coordinate. Over each base complement matching split the full K4,4 into four matchings. These are disjoint and cover precisely the complement.

Finally, the lifted union of the first two matchings still has a cycle of length not divisible by 3. The affine holonomy around the original length-L cycle has scalar w^L != 1, hence has one fixed point and one orbit of length 3. The lifted cycles have lengths L and 3L, so the length-L cycle persists. This proves all hypotheses needed to iterate the lift.

### Degree interpolation lemma

Let h be the four-fold lift of G. Select k whole perfect matchings of G (0 <= k <= d). Over those base edges replace the designated matching by its complement in K4,4. This raises the degree by 2k. Select j whole perfect matchings of the base complement (0 <= j <= m-1-d), and insert full K4,4 blocks there, raising the degree by 4j. No edges are duplicated and no loops are added.

A full fibre has label sum zero in both coordinates: the first is repeated four times and the sum of all F4 elements is zero. Therefore a matching and its three-edge complement contribute the same label sum at each vertex, and full blocks contribute zero. The graph keeps its original open or closed zero-XOR type and has degree d+2k+4j.

If k=0, it contains the connected lift h. If k>0, any replaced block K4,4 minus a matching is connected, so all four vertices in each of its endpoint fibres are mutually connected. A matching or a triple block over any adjacent base edge propagates this property to the next fibre. Since the original quotient G is connected, the entire graph is connected. Added full blocks cannot hurt connectivity.

As k,j vary, these degrees cover every integer of the parity of d from d to 4m-4-d. After dividing the increments by 2 this is the union of intervals [2j,2j+d]; consecutive intervals overlap since d >= 4.

### Seeds and induction

For powers 4 and 5 use closed degree-4 and open degree-5 seeds, together with certified perfect matching decompositions of each seed and its complement. All are exactly checked, and the distinguished unions have cycle lengths:

* m=16, closed degree 4: [16]. Graph: outputs/base-16-4-1.json.
* m=16, open degree 5: [16]. Graph: ../expanded-corpus-r90/outputs/xor-16-5.json (immutable hashed input).
* m=32, closed degree 4: [32]. Graph: outputs/seed-32-4-1.json, the complement of the authors' open degree-27 example.
* m=32, open degree 5: [8,16,8]. Graph: outputs/seed-32-5-0.json, the authors' example.

The matching certificates have corresponding *-factors-0.json and *-factors-1.json names in outputs/. All decomposition edges, degrees, simplicity, identity label sums and connectivity are checked by exact integer operations; no floating-point solver conclusion is trusted as a proof of feasibility. The solver only proposes finite edge/matching lists.

The lift lemma inductively produces such low-degree seeds at every n >= 4 (separately in each parity of n). At N=2^n with n >= 6, interpolation from the seeds at m=N/4 gives open degrees 5,7,...,N-9 and closed degrees 4,6,...,N-8. The missing open degrees N-7 and N-5 are complements of the constructed closed degrees 6 and 4. The missing corrected closed degree N-6 is the complement of constructed open degree 5. Every complement used here has degree at least N/2 and is connected: if disconnected, each component would have at least degree+1 vertices, impossible for two components on N vertices. The XOR complement identity proves the desired types.

For n=4 Theorems 17 and 18 give all corrected degrees. Local exact certificates also cover all of them via cached open degrees 5 and 7, the fetched author open degree 9, and the local closed degree 4 and their complements.

For n=5, the source and local certificates cover open degrees 5,7,9,11,13,15,27 and their closed complements. The local closed graphs of degrees 8,10,12,14 give open degrees 23,21,19,17. Finally outputs/symmetric-32-6.json is a closed degree-6 graph, whose complement has open degree 25. Its exact verification includes connectivity of both graphs. It was found by imposing the order-3 label symmetry that cycles low-bit values 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 1 and fixes low-bit value 0; there are 184 edge orbits. This closes every corrected base case. The symmetry is only a search aid, not a hypothesis of the theorem.

Thus there are no remaining ordinary mathematical parameter gaps in the corrected theorem, subject to independent review of the general lemmas above. There is no way to append the literal closed degree N-4.

Python exact verification and negative controls are separate evidence, not formalization. No Lean packet is asserted. {
  "mathdb_id": 372205,
  "title": "Existence of regular open and closed XOR-magic graphs of power-of-two order",
  "statement": "Let $n$ be a positive integer, and let $d$ be a degree. An **open XOR-magic graph** and a **closed XOR-magic graph** are graphs admitting, respectively, an open or closed XOR-magic labeling. The graphs below are required to have order $2^n$.

For each degree

$$
d\in\{5,7,\ldots,2^n-7,2^n-5\},
$$

there exists a $d$-regular open XOR-magic graph of order $2^n$. For each degree

$$
d\in\{4,6,\ldots,2^n-6,2^n-4\},
$$

there exists a $d$-regular closed XOR-magic graph of order $2^n$.

**Existence conjecture.** For every permitted degree $d$ in the two displayed sets, the corresponding regular open or closed XOR-magic graph exists. This would complete the existence picture apart from the degrees excluded by the previously stated nonexistence result and extend the constructions known for order $16$ and order $8$ to every order that is a power of two.",

# Independent adversarial review: MathDB 372205 (arXiv:2512.19278, Conjecture 25)

Reviewer lane: xor-magic-review-r1. Date: 2026-11-02 UTC (2026-11-01 Los Angeles). No child agents, no git, no shared-ledger edits, no uploads or messages. All writes stayed in this lane. xor-magic-formal-r3 was not touched. Credit: 0. This is a review, not an acceptance.

The 286 input files were hash-bound before and after the work, with an unchanged aggregate of `0d0d7a3d…15c0f1`. PROOF.md and the r2 zip match the pinned SHA-256 values.

## Verdicts

| Gate | Verdict |
|---|---|
| A. Source fidelity and scope | QUALIFIED_PASS |
| B. Ordinary mathematics | PASS |
| C. Partial Lean packets (r2 replay and fidelity) | PASS as a partial packet; not a solution |
| D. Prior art | QUALIFIED_PASS (Batal's article body unread) |
| E. Significance | QUALIFIED_PASS |

Recommendation: continue the formalization. There is no credit until a kernel-checked endpoint proves both `∀ n ≥ 4, ¬ PrintedAt n` and `∀ n ≥ 4, CorrectedAt n`, with a fresh strict extracted replay.

## A. Scope

The source definition requires:
- a simple, connected graph of order 2^n;
- a bijective labelling onto (Z_2)^n;
- zero open or closed neighbourhood sums.

Conjecture 25 does not quantify n. The context fixes n ≥ 4 (Theorem 5 is stated for n > 3).

The printed closed list {4, …, 2^n-6, 2^n-4} contains 2^n-4, which Proposition 24 forbids. So the printed statement is false for every n ≥ 3; at n = 3 the closed list is {4} = 2^3-4. I re-proved the obstruction by hand. The complement of such a graph is cubic and open-zero. At a neighbour of the label-0 vertex, the two remaining neighbours would need equal labels, which contradicts injectivity. The argument does not use connectivity.

Several things show that the corrected range is the intended statement:
- The printed open list is exactly the odd degrees not excluded by Proposition 24.
- Under Observation 1 (d ↦ 2^n-1-d), the open list maps to closed {4, …, 2^n-6}, not {4, …, 2^n-4}.
- Theorem 18 at n = 4 stops at 10 = 2^n-6, and Section 4 calls this "each possible degree".
- MathDB's own sentence says the conjecture completes the picture "apart from the degrees excluded by the previously stated nonexistence result".

Section 4 has two more typos: the exclusion set {0, 2, 2^n-2, 2^n}, and "odd degree" used for an even list. Neither counts as a discovery.

Judgement: the literal negation together with the corrected theorem is a full resolution of the problem's intended scope. It is not a zero-credit endpoint correction, because the correction deletes only one degree that the source itself already forbids, and all the substantive existence content is what gets proved. Root must present the credited claim exactly in this form.

MathDB's wording omits "connected". The existence direction is unaffected. For the negation, I proved a connectivity-free obstruction in Lean (see C).

## B. Mathematics

I checked every lemma by hand and with code written from scratch (`scripts/xm.py`). My code chooses c at random in ker B, unlike the focused lane's deterministic first-basis-vector rule.

- **Lift lemma.** The labelling is a bijection onto F2^(n+2). The linear coefficient is (d-2) + w + w^-1 + ε ≡ d-1+ε ≡ 0 (mod 2). This needs every cycle of F oriented so that each vertex has one F-edge in and one out. The constant term is Bc, where column e of B is 1 at the tail and a^-1 at the head. Both ker D = 0 and rank B = m follow from the w^L transport. So dim ker B = (d/2-1)m ≥ m.
- **Dimension count.** For each edge, the BD entry is exactly 1, so BD ≠ 0. That gives dim(im D ∩ ker B) ≤ m-1. Measured values (dim ker B versus the intersection):
  - closed, d = 4: 16 vs 8 at m = 16; 32 vs 6 at m = 32; 64 vs 12 at m = 64;
  - open, d = 5: 24 vs 6; 48 vs 6; 96 vs 10.
  - The d = 4 boundary therefore holds with margin.
- **Holonomy.** The translation subgroup is normal and stable under t ↦ wt, so it has order 1 or 4; order 2 is impossible. With no translations, H is cyclic of order 3 with a common fixed point. That point transports to a section b with c = Db, which contradicts the choice of c.
  - I tested "connected ⇔ c ∉ im D" in 160 control lifts: c = 0, c in im D ∩ ker B, and random c in ker B. Every one agreed.
- **Persistence.** The lifted complement splits into 3 + 3d + 4(m-1-d) = 4m-1-d perfect matchings. I verified this exactly at every lift level built. The distinguished cycle lifts to lengths L and 3L. Observed examples:
  - [16] → [16, 48];
  - [8, 8, 16] → [8, 8, 16, 24, 24, 48];
  - at the second level, [16, 48] → [16, 48, 96, 96].
- **Interpolation.** The degree is d+2k+4j, and these values cover every degree of the right parity in [d, 4m-4-d]. Label sums are preserved. Connectivity holds for k = 0 (the graph contains the lift) and for k > 0 (K4,4 minus a matching is the cube, which is connected).
- **Complements and induction.** The endpoints come from complements: open N-5 and N-7 from closed 4 and 6, and closed N-6 from open 5. The induction runs n → n+2 in both parities.

Independent computations (corroboration, not proof):

| n | Degrees verified | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| 6 | 56 of 56 | every corrected degree |
| 7 | 120 of 120 | every corrected degree |
| 8 | 248 of 248 | two lift iterations, 16 → 64 → 256 |
| 9 | 51 of 504 | every endpoint, plus 40 random degrees |

Every graph listed was checked to be simple, regular, zero-sum and connected.

At orders 16 and 32, I checked every base witness and complement independently. The author files were parsed by AST literals, never executed. Every corrected degree is covered, and the seed matching certificates are valid.

Objections (exposition only):

1. PROOF.md attributes the n = 4 closed-6 and n = 5 closed-4 cases to complements. Those complements have degree below N/2, so the high-degree lemma does not apply. They are in fact connected (verified here), and the Lean bases have direct certificates.
2. The equivalence "the holonomies form a group, and connectivity ⇔ transitivity" is used without proof.

## C. Lean r2 packet

- **Extraction.** Fresh extraction into `work/replay-r2` with my own driver (`scripts/lean_replay.py`); the packet's own `replay.py` was not run.
  - The zip's SHA-256 matches the pinned value.
  - All 72 members are regular files with relative paths.
  - The zip contained no oleans.
  - All 48 Lean sources are byte-identical to the lane's copies.
- **Strict build.** Lean 4.34.1 (commit 5045d005…). All 48 modules build with `-j1 -DwarningAsError=true`, each call under its own cap scope. The peak was 29.9 s wall and 5.06 GB sampled private RSS.
- **leanchecker.** 48 of 48 pass.
- **My own audit** (`lean/ReviewAudit.lean`) covers 780 declarations, 502 of them theorems. None is an axiom, opaque, unsafe, partial, `implemented_by` or `extern`. Transitive axioms are only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
- **Negative controls.** All six packet controls fail for the stated reason. My two extra controls also fail as intended:
  - the degree-10 witness does not inhabit `ClosedExists 4 12`;
  - `PrintedAt 4` cannot be obtained from `CorrectedAt 4`.
- **Definitional fidelity.** `Bits`, `OpenMagic`, `ClosedMagic`, `OpenExists`, `ClosedExists`, `PrintedAt` and `CorrectedAt` faithfully render the source definitions and both statements. I found no weakening. Notes:
  - The packet's negations instantiate only n = 4.
  - My `lean/ReviewControls.lean` compiles strictly with the standard axioms and proves:
    - `∀ n ≥ 3, ¬ PrintedAt n`;
    - a connectivity-free version of the 2^n-4 obstruction;
    - `CorrectedAt 4 ∧ CorrectedAt 5 ∧ ¬ PrintedAt 4 ∧ ¬ PrintedAt 5`.
  - There is no universal or conditional `CorrectedAt` theorem, as GAPS.md honestly says.

## D. Prior art

What I read:
- 2512.19278 v1 (re-fetched: still only v1).
- Batal, arXiv:2609.05934 (September 2026). It does not cite 2512.19278 or treat Conjecture 25; its XOR-magic paragraph is only about row-separation characterisations.
- Siehler 2019, author copy. It covers cubic closed graphs only.
- Batal's GCGT 2026 abstract. It covers the other parity class: closed odd degrees 3 … 2^n-5 and 2^n-1, plus nonexistence for 2^n-3.
- Two 2026 abstracts by Cichacz, Grochowski and Zuazua. They claim only Theorem 5-level existence.

What stayed unread:
- The body of Batal's DAM 2026 article. The ScienceDirect 403 route was not retried; the IYTE repository returned an Anubis bot challenge, which I did not solve or retry; no arXiv version exists; a ResearchGate item was seen in search results but not fetched.
- OpenAlex's "cites" lists are empty, but incomplete, so they are not clearance.

Registries (HEAD identity only):
- openai/math HEAD is `4eaee875…`, unchanged.
- Omega HEAD is now `da784eaf…` (2026-11-02T02:10Z); its latest change is unrelated.

I found no existing all-degree construction. Batal posed odd-open and even-closed existence as an open problem, so his paper cannot contain the result.

## E. Significance

Qualified pass. The result settles the source's only conjecture, in its intended form, for every n and every degree. With Proposition 24 it gives a complete if-and-only-if picture within the parity classes. The source's own tools (products, complements and MILP bases) leave large gaps; at n = 8, for example, the source lists only open degrees 9–21 plus sporadic high degrees. The F4 affine lift is a new uniform mechanism, so the result is not a routine corollary, padding or a parameter instance.

The qualifications:
- the problem is recent and from a small community, and the proof is short;
- credit depends on root accepting the scope framing in A;
- credit also depends on the missing Lean endpoint;
- Batal's article body is unread.

## Hazards the formalization must avoid

- **H1.** The distinguished cycle needs length ≥ 3 and must be a genuine cycle of F. A back-and-forth closed walk of length 2 satisfies 3 ∤ 2 but has trivial holonomy.
- **H2.** Every cycle of F must be oriented consistently, and the distinguished cycle traversed in that orientation. Otherwise the holonomy scalar is w^(fwd-bwd). All non-F edges must have slope exactly 1.
- **H3.** B and D must use the same oriented edges. The reverse edge map is a^-1 x + a^-1 c. The nonzero BD witness needs simplicity. Use |E| = dm/2 ≥ 2m.
- **H4.** The lifted complement must be split into exactly 4m-1-d disjoint matchings that cover it. The next distinguished cycle is the fixed-point lift.
- **H5.** Interpolation connectivity needs separate k = 0 and k > 0 arguments. Full blocks go over base-complement matchings only.
- **H6.** Base complements of degree below N/2 need direct connectivity certificates.
- **H7.** The induction runs n → n+2 from n = 4 and from n = 5 separately; the interpolation base needs n ≥ 6.

## Artifacts

- `review.json` — machine-readable verdicts, objections and next actions.
- `scripts/` — `xm.py`, `verify_base.py`, `lift_check.py`, `lean_replay.py`, `capped.py`, `hashbind.py`, `fetch.py`.
- `lean/` — the reviewer audit, positive controls and negative controls.
- `outputs/` — base verification and lift results for n = 6, 7, 8 and 9.
- `receipts/` — input hashes before and after, per-call cap receipts, Lean replay state, web receipts.
- `logs/` — logs for every call.
- `work/` — the fresh extraction (with built oleans) and the fetched web bodies, kept as untrusted data.

No background jobs remain from this lane. The Lean processes visible on the machine belong to the sibling r3 lane.

import LiftGraph
noncomputable section
namespace XorMagic

def scalar (s : Fin 3) (x : Four) : Four :=
  if s = 0 then x else if s = 1 then omegaMap x else omegaSq x

theorem scalar_add : ∀ s x y, scalar s (x+y) = scalar s x + scalar s y := by decide

def inverseScalar (s : Fin 3) : Fin 3 := if s = 0 then 0 else if s = 1 then 2 else 1

def affineThree (s : Fin 3) (c : Four) : Four ≃ Four where
  toFun x := scalar s x + c
  invFun y := scalar (inverseScalar s) (y+c)
  left_inv := by revert s c; decide
  right_inv := by revert s c; decide

variable {m : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin m)) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
/-- One representative of each undirected edge, ordered by the vertex index. -/
abbrev OrientedEdge := {p : Fin m × Fin m // p.1 < p.2 ∧ G.Adj p.1 p.2}

def orientedMap (e : OrientedEdge G → Four ≃ Four) (u v : Fin m) : Four ≃ Four :=
  if h : u < v ∧ G.Adj u v then e ⟨(u,v),h⟩
  else if h : v < u ∧ G.Adj v u then (e ⟨(v,u),h⟩).symm
  else Equiv.refl Four

theorem orientedMap_reverse (e : OrientedEdge G → Four ≃ Four) {u v : Fin m}
    (h : G.Adj u v) (x : Four) :
    orientedMap G e v u (orientedMap G e u v x) = x := by
  have hn : u ≠ v := h.ne
  rcases lt_or_gt_of_ne hn with hl | hl
  · simp [orientedMap, hl, h, h.symm, not_lt.mpr (le_of_lt hl)]
  · simp [orientedMap, hl, h, h.symm, not_lt.mpr (le_of_lt hl)]

/-- The actual four-fold affine graph, with one scalar and constant per oriented edge. -/
def affineTransport (s : OrientedEdge G → Fin 3) (c : OrientedEdge G → Four) :
    EdgeTransport G where
  map := orientedMap G (fun e => affineThree (s e) (c e))
  reverse := orientedMap_reverse G _

theorem forward_affine (s : OrientedEdge G → Fin 3) (c : OrientedEdge G → Four)
    (e : OrientedEdge G) (x : Four) :
    (affineTransport G s c).map e.val.1 e.val.2 x = scalar (s e) x + c e := by
  simp [affineTransport, orientedMap, e.property, affineThree]
end XorMagic

namespace XorMagic
variable {m n d : ℕ} {G : SimpleGraph (Fin m)} [DecidableRel G.Adj]
/-- The complement factors required by the chosen lift are supplied by the
three disjoint block families, for every translation. -/
noncomputable def ColouredSeed.complementInput {closed : Bool}
    (S : ColouredSeed G n d closed) (c : OrientedEdge G → Four) :
    LiftComplementInput G (chosenSlopes G S.colouring) c d := by
  have hcard : d+1 ≤ m := by
    have hm : Nonempty (Fin m) := by
      have h := S.seed.magic
      cases closed <;> exact h.1.nonempty
    obtain ⟨v⟩ := hm
    have hh := G.degree_lt_card_verts v
    rw [S.seed.regular v] at hh
    simpa using hh
  refine ⟨?_⟩
  have h := (affineTransport G (chosenSlopes G S.colouring) c).complementMatching_exact
    S.seed.factorCycle.factors S.seed.factorCycle.complementFactors (by simpa using hcard)
  simpa [Fintype.card_prod, Fintype.card_fin, show Fintype.card Four = 4 by decide,
    Nat.mul_comm] using h

/-- Product-type assembly with no complement hypothesis remaining. -/
theorem chosen_seed_product [Nonempty (Fin m)] {closed : Bool}
    (S : ColouredSeed G n d closed) (hd : 4 ≤ d)
    (hparity : if closed then Even d else Odd d) :
    ∃ c : OrientedEdge G → Four,
      Nonempty (ColouredLiftSeed (affineTransport G (chosenSlopes G S.colouring) c).graph
        (n+2) d closed) :=
  chosen_seed_lift_data S hd hparity S.complementInput
end XorMagic

def binaryLabel (n : ℕ) (v : Fin (2^n)) : Bits n :=
  fun i => if v.val.testBit i.val then 1 else 0

theorem connected_of_descent {N : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin N))
    (root : Fin N) (parent : Fin N → Fin N) (rank : Fin N → ℕ)
    (h : ∀ v, v ≠ root → G.Adj v (parent v) ∧ rank (parent v) < rank v) :
    G.Connected := by
  have hr : ∀ k v, rank v = k → G.Reachable root v := by
    intro k
    induction k using Nat.strong_induction_on with
    | h k ih =>
      intro v hv
      by_cases he : v = root
      · subst v; exact SimpleGraph.Reachable.refl root
      · obtain ⟨ha, hl⟩ := h v he
        exact (ih (rank (parent v)) (by omega) (parent v) rfl).trans ha.symm.reachable
  exact G.connected_iff_exists_forall_reachable.mpr ⟨root, fun v => hr (rank v) v rfl⟩

def maskGraph {N : ℕ} (mask : Fin N → ℕ)
    (sym : ∀ u v, (mask u).testBit v.val = (mask v).testBit u.val)
    (loop : ∀ u, (mask u).testBit u.val = false) : SimpleGraph (Fin N) where
  Adj u v := (mask u).testBit v.val = true
  symm := ⟨by intro u v h; rw [sym v u]; exact h⟩
  loopless := ⟨by intro u h; simp [loop u] at h⟩

instance maskGraphDecidable {N : ℕ} (mask : Fin N → ℕ) (sym) (loop) :
    DecidableRel (maskGraph mask sym loop).Adj := fun _ _ => inferInstanceAs (Decidable (_ = true))

end XorMagic

  colour : V → Bool

  proper1 : ∀ v, colour v ≠ colour (F.mate ⟨1, by omega⟩ v)

variable {F : MatchingDecomposition G d} {hd : 2 ≤ d} (b : FactorColouring F hd)
def directed (u v : V) : Fin 3 :=
  if F.mate ⟨0, by omega⟩ u = v then (if b.colour u then 1 else 2)
  else if F.mate ⟨1, by omega⟩ u = v then (if b.colour u then 2 else 1)
  else 0

theorem mate_reverse (i : Fin d) (u v : V) : F.mate i u = v ↔ F.mate i v = u := by
  constructor <;> intro h
  · rw [← h, F.involutive]
  · rw [← h, F.involutive]

omit [Fintype V] in
theorem reverse (u v : V) : b.directed v u = inverseScalar (b.directed u v) := by
  have h0 := mate_reverse (F := F) ⟨0, by omega⟩ u v
  have h1 := mate_reverse (F := F) ⟨1, by omega⟩ u v
  unfold directed
  by_cases e0 : F.mate ⟨0, by omega⟩ u = v
  · have bc := b.proper0 u
    rw [e0] at bc
    simp only [h0.mp e0, e0, ite_true]
    cases hu : b.colour u <;> cases hv : b.colour v <;> simp_all <;> decide
  · by_cases e1 : F.mate ⟨1, by omega⟩ u = v
    · have bc := b.proper1 u

        e1, h1.mp e1, ite_true, ite_false]
      cases hu : b.colour u <;> cases hv : b.colour v <;> simp_all <;> decide
    · simp only [e0,e1,show ¬ F.mate ⟨0, by omega⟩ v = u from fun h => e0 (h0.mpr h),
        show ¬ F.mate ⟨1, by omega⟩ v = u from fun h => e1 (h1.mpr h), ite_false]

variable {m d : ℕ} {G : SimpleGraph (Fin m)} [DecidableRel G.Adj]
variable {F : MatchingDecomposition G d} {hd : 2 ≤ d} (b : FactorColouring F hd)
theorem omegaWalk_step {u v : Fin m} (p : G.Walk u v)
    (h : OmegaWalk G (chosenSlopes G b) p) {i : ℕ} (hi : i < p.length) :
    b.directed (p.getVert i) (p.getVert (i+1)) = 1 := by
  induction p generalizing i with
  | nil => simp at hi
  | @cons u v w ha p ih =>
    cases i with
    | zero => simpa only [SimpleGraph.Walk.getVert, SimpleGraph.Walk.getVert_zero] using (chosen_outgoing G b ha).symm.trans h.1
    | succ i => exact ih h.2 (by simpa using hi)

variable {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] {H : SimpleGraph V}
variable {e : ℕ} {D : MatchingDecomposition H e} {he : 2 ≤ e}
/-- Directed colours lift on every actual edge, not just distinguished edges. -/
theorem FactorColouring.directed_lift (a : FactorColouring D he) (T : EdgeTransport H)
    {p q : V × Four} (hpq : T.graph.Adj p q) :
    (a.lift T).directed p q = a.directed p.1 q.1 := by
  have hm (i : Fin e) : (T.matching D).mate i p = q ↔ D.mate i p.1 = q.1 := by
    constructor
    · intro h; exact congrArg Prod.fst h
    · intro h
      apply Prod.ext h
      change T.map p.1 (D.mate i p.1) p.2 = q.2
      rw [h]; exact hpq.2
  simp only [FactorColouring.directed, hm]
  rfl

/-- Indexed oriented cycles, usable before and after lifting and relabelling. -/
structure ColouredCycleData (H : SimpleGraph V) (e : ℕ) extends StrongFactorCycleData H e where
  colouring : FactorColouring factors two_le
  outgoing : ∀ i, colouring.directed (cycle i)
    (cycle ⟨(i.val+1)%length, Nat.mod_lt _ positive⟩) = 1

def ColouredSeed.colouredCycle {closed : Bool} (S : ColouredSeed G n d closed) :
    ColouredCycleData G d where
  toStrongFactorCycleData := S.strongCycle
  colouring := S.colouring
  outgoing i := by
    dsimp [ColouredSeed.strongCycle] at i ⊢
    have hs := omegaWalk_step S.colouring S.walk S.oriented (i := i.val) (by rw [S.length_eq]; exact i.isLt)

        simpa only [← S.length_eq, he] using (SimpleGraph.Walk.getVert_length S.walk)

/-- A seed with a colouring and a genuine oriented distinguished cycle.
The indexed cycle and walk are tied vertex by vertex. -/
structure ColouredSeed {m : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin m)) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (n d : ℕ) (closed : Bool) where
  seed : LiftSeed G n d closed
  strong : 3 ≤ seed.factorCycle.length
  colouring : FactorColouring seed.factorCycle.factors seed.factorCycle.two_le
  walk : G.Walk (seed.factorCycle.cycle ⟨0,seed.factorCycle.positive⟩)
    (seed.factorCycle.cycle ⟨0,seed.factorCycle.positive⟩)
  isCycle : walk.IsCycle
  length_eq : walk.length = seed.factorCycle.length
  indexed : ∀ i : Fin seed.factorCycle.length, walk.getVert i.val = seed.factorCycle.cycle i
  starts_true : colouring.colour (seed.factorCycle.cycle ⟨0,seed.factorCycle.positive⟩) = true
  oriented : OmegaWalk G (chosenSlopes G colouring) walk

def ColouredSeed.strongCycle {m n d : ℕ} {G : SimpleGraph (Fin m)} [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    {closed : Bool} (S : ColouredSeed G n d closed) : StrongFactorCycleData G d where
  toFactorCycleData := S.seed.factorCycle
  three_le := S.strong

def FactorColouring.lift {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    {G : SimpleGraph V} {d : ℕ} {F : MatchingDecomposition G d} {hd : 2 ≤ d}
    (b : FactorColouring F hd) (T : EdgeTransport G) : FactorColouring (T.matching F) hd where
  colour p := b.colour p.1
  proper0 p := b.proper0 p.1
  proper1 p := b.proper1 p.1

abbrev NonzeroFour := {a : Four // a ≠ 0}
theorem four_add_self (a : Four) : a + a = 0 := by revert a; decide
theorem nonzeroFour_card : Fintype.card NonzeroFour = 3 := by decide

def fibreMatching (V : Type) (a : NonzeroFour) (p : V × Four) : V × Four :=
  (p.1, p.2 + a.1)
theorem fibreMatching_involutive (V : Type) (a : NonzeroFour) :
    Function.Involutive (fibreMatching V a) := by
  intro p; simp [fibreMatching, add_assoc, four_add_self]
theorem fibreMatching_no_fixed (V : Type) (a : NonzeroFour)
    (p : V × Four) : fibreMatching V a p ≠ p := by
  intro h
  have h' : p.2 + a.1 = p.2 + 0 := by simpa [fibreMatching] using congrArg Prod.snd h
  exact a.2 (add_left_cancel h')
theorem fibreMatching_distinct (V : Type) (p : V × Four) :
    Function.Injective (fun a : NonzeroFour => fibreMatching V a p) := by
  intro a b h
  apply Subtype.ext
  exact add_left_cancel (congrArg Prod.snd h)
theorem fibreMatching_cover {V : Type} (p q : V × Four) :
    (p.1 = q.1 ∧ p.2 ≠ q.2) ↔ ∃ a : NonzeroFour, fibreMatching V a p = q := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨h,h'⟩
    exact ⟨⟨q.2-p.2, sub_ne_zero.mpr (Ne.symm h')⟩, Prod.ext h (by simp [fibreMatching])⟩
  · rintro ⟨a,h⟩
    change (p.1, p.2 + a.1) = q at h
    have hf : p.1 = q.1 := by simpa only using congrArg Prod.fst h
    refine ⟨hf, ?_⟩
    intro he

    (i : Fin d) (a : Four) (p : V × Four) : V × Four :=
  (F.mate i p.1, (C i (F.mate i p.1)).symm (C i p.1 p.2 + a))
theorem blockMate_involutive {V : Type} {d : ℕ} {G : SimpleGraph V} [Fintype V]
    (F : MatchingDecomposition G d) (C : Fin d → V → Four ≃ Four)
    (i : Fin d) (a : Four) : Function.Involutive (blockMate F C i a) := by
  intro p
  apply Prod.ext
  · exact F.involutive i p.1

    (F : MatchingDecomposition G d) (C : Fin d → V → Four ≃ Four)
    (i : Fin d) (a : Four) (p : V × Four) : blockMate F C i a p ≠ p := by

def involutionGraph (f : I → W → W) (hinv : ∀ i, Function.Involutive (f i))
    (hfree : ∀ i w, f i w ≠ w) : SimpleGraph W where
  Adj v w := ∃ i, f i v = w
  symm := ⟨by rintro v w ⟨i,hi⟩; exact ⟨i,hi ▸ hinv i v⟩⟩
  loopless := ⟨by rintro v ⟨i,hi⟩; exact hfree i v hi⟩

    (hfree : ∀ i w, f i w ≠ w) : DecidableRel (involutionGraph f hinv hfree).Adj := Classical.decRel _
theorem involutionGraph_degree (f : I → W → W) (hinv : ∀ i, Function.Involutive (f i))
    (hfree : ∀ i w, f i w ≠ w) (hdis : ∀ w, Function.Injective (fun i => f i w)) :
    (involutionGraph f hinv hfree).IsRegularOfDegree (Fintype.card I) := by
  classical
  intro w
  rw [← SimpleGraph.card_neighborFinset_eq_degree]
  have he : (involutionGraph f hinv hfree).neighborFinset w = Finset.univ.image (fun i => f i w) := by
    ext v
    rw [SimpleGraph.mem_neighborFinset]
    simp [involutionGraph]
  rw [he, Finset.card_image_of_injective _ (hdis w), Finset.card_univ]

  · have h : (i,a.1) = (l,b.1) := blockMate_distinct F (T.matchingChart F) p (by exact he)
    have hi : i = l := congrArg Prod.fst h
    subst l
    exact congrArg Sum.inl (by congr 1; exact Subtype.ext (by simpa only using congrArg Prod.snd h))
  · have hv : F.mate i p.1 = H.mate ⟨l.val,lt_of_lt_of_le l.isLt hj⟩ p.1 := congrArg Prod.fst he
    have hg := (F.cover p.1 _).mpr ⟨i,rfl⟩

    have hg := (F.cover p.1 _).mpr ⟨l,rfl⟩

def projection : T.graph →g G where
  toFun := Prod.fst
  map_rel' h := h.1

/-- Lift a walk with a specified initial fibre point. -/
def liftWalk {u v : V} (p : G.Walk u v) (x : Four) :
    T.graph.Walk (u,x) (v,T.along p x) := by
  induction p generalizing x with
  | nil => exact .nil
  | @cons u v w h p ih => exact .cons ⟨h,rfl⟩ (ih (T.map u v x))

theorem length_liftWalk {u v : V} (p : G.Walk u v) (x : Four) :
    (T.liftWalk p x).length = p.length := by
  induction p generalizing x with
  | nil => rfl
  | @cons u v w h p ih =>
    change (T.liftWalk p (T.map u v x)).length + 1 = p.length + 1
    exact congrArg (fun n => n+1) (ih _)

theorem map_liftWalk {u v : V} (p : G.Walk u v) (x : Four) :
    (T.liftWalk p x).map T.projection = p := by
  induction p generalizing x with
  | nil => rfl
  | @cons u v w h p ih =>
    change SimpleGraph.Walk.cons h ((T.liftWalk p (T.map u v x)).map T.projection) = SimpleGraph.Walk.cons h p
    exact congrArg (SimpleGraph.Walk.cons h) (ih _)

def closedLift {v : V} (p : G.Walk v v) (x : Four) (hx : T.along p x = x) :
    T.graph.Walk (v,x) (v,x) :=
  (T.liftWalk p x).copy rfl (Prod.ext rfl hx)

    (T.closedLift p x hx).length = p.length := by
  simp only [closedLift, SimpleGraph.Walk.length_copy, T.length_liftWalk]

theorem map_closedLift {v : V} (p : G.Walk v v) (x : Four) (hx : T.along p x = x) :
    (T.closedLift p x hx).map T.projection = p := by
  simp only [closedLift, SimpleGraph.Walk.map_copy, T.map_liftWalk]
  rfl

theorem isCycle_closedLift {v : V} (p : G.Walk v v) (hp : p.IsCycle)

  apply SimpleGraph.Walk.IsCycle.of_map (f := T.projection)

  @Finset.filter Four (fun x => T.graph.Reachable r (v,x)) (Classical.decPred _) Finset.univ

theorem mem_fibre (r : V × Four) (v : V) (x : Four) :
    x ∈ T.fibre r v ↔ T.graph.Reachable r (v,x) := by
  classical
  simp [fibre]

theorem fibre_transport (r : V × Four) {u v : V} (h : G.Adj u v) (x : Four) :
    x ∈ T.fibre r u ↔ T.map u v x ∈ T.fibre r v := by
  rw [T.mem_fibre, T.mem_fibre]
  have edge : T.graph.Adj (u,x) (v,T.map u v x) := ⟨h,rfl⟩
  exact ⟨fun hr => hr.trans edge.reachable, fun hr => hr.trans edge.symm.reachable⟩

  toFun x := ⟨T.map u v x, (T.fibre_transport r h x).mp x.property⟩
  invFun y := ⟨T.map v u y, (T.fibre_transport r h.symm y).mp y.property⟩
  left_inv x := Subtype.ext (T.reverse h x)
  right_inv y := Subtype.ext (T.reverse h.symm y)

  simpa using Fintype.card_congr (T.fibreEquiv r h)

    (T.fibre r u).card = (T.fibre r v).card := by
  obtain ⟨p⟩ := h
  induction p with
  | nil => rfl
  | cons h _ ih => exact (T.fibre_card_adj r h).trans ih

  rw [← T.fibre_card_reachable r (hG.preconnected r.1 v)]
  exact Finset.card_pos.mpr ⟨r.2,h⟩

  intro p q

    apply Finset.eq_univ_of_card

variable {V : Type} [Fintype V] {G : SimpleGraph V}

/-- The transports are specified in both directions, with an inverse law on every edge. -/
structure EdgeTransport (G : SimpleGraph V) where
  map : V → V → Four ≃ Four
  reverse : ∀ {u v}, G.Adj u v → ∀ x, map v u (map u v x) = x

namespace EdgeTransport
variable (T : EdgeTransport G)

def graph : SimpleGraph (V × Four) where
  Adj p q := G.Adj p.1 q.1 ∧ T.map p.1 q.1 p.2 = q.2
  symm := ⟨by
    intro p q h
    exact ⟨h.1.symm, h.2 ▸ T.reverse h.1 p.2⟩⟩
  loopless := ⟨by intro p h; exact G.irrefl h.1⟩

instance [DecidableRel G.Adj] : DecidableRel T.graph.Adj :=
  fun _ _ => inferInstanceAs (Decidable (_ ∧ _))

def neighborEmbedding (v : V) (x : Four) : V ↪ V × Four where
  toFun u := (u, T.map v u x)
  inj' := by intro a b h; exact congrArg Prod.fst h

theorem neighbors [DecidableRel G.Adj] (v : V) (x : Four) :
    T.graph.neighborFinset (v,x) = (G.neighborFinset v).map (T.neighborEmbedding v x) := by
  ext ⟨u,y⟩
  rw [SimpleGraph.mem_neighborFinset, Finset.mem_map]
  change (G.Adj v u ∧ T.map v u x = y) ↔
    ∃ a, a ∈ G.neighborFinset v ∧ (a,T.map v a x) = (u,y)
  simp only [SimpleGraph.mem_neighborFinset]
  constructor
  · intro ⟨h,e⟩; exact ⟨u,h,Prod.ext rfl e⟩
  · rintro ⟨a,h,e⟩
    have ha : a = u := congrArg Prod.fst e
    subst a
    exact ⟨h,congrArg Prod.snd e⟩

theorem degree [DecidableRel G.Adj] (p : V × Four) : T.graph.degree p = G.degree p.1 := by
  rw [← SimpleGraph.card_neighborFinset_eq_degree, T.neighbors,
    Finset.card_map, SimpleGraph.card_neighborFinset_eq_degree]

theorem regular [DecidableRel G.Adj] {d : ℕ} (h : G.IsRegularOfDegree d) :
    T.graph.IsRegularOfDegree d := fun p => (T.degree p).trans (h p.1)

theorem sum_neighbors [DecidableRel G.Adj] {A : Type*} [AddCommMonoid A]
    (f : V × Four → A) (v : V) (x : Four) :
    ∑ p ∈ T.graph.neighborFinset (v,x), f p =
      ∑ u ∈ G.neighborFinset v, f (u,T.map v u x) := by
  rw [T.neighbors, Finset.sum_map]; rfl

theorem sum_first [DecidableRel G.Adj] {n : ℕ} (l : V → Bits n) (v : V) (x : Four) :
    ∑ p ∈ T.graph.neighborFinset (v,x), l p.1 = ∑ u ∈ G.neighborFinset v, l u :=
  T.sum_neighbors _ v x

def matching {d : ℕ} (F : MatchingDecomposition G d) : MatchingDecomposition T.graph d where
  mate i p := (F.mate i p.1, T.map p.1 (F.mate i p.1) p.2)
  involutive i p := by
    have ha : G.Adj p.1 (F.mate i p.1) := (F.cover _ _).mpr ⟨i,rfl⟩
    apply Prod.ext
    · exact F.involutive i p.1
    · simpa only [F.involutive] using T.reverse ha p.2
  no_fixed i p h := F.no_fixed i p.1 (congrArg Prod.fst h)
  distinct p i j h := F.distinct p.1 (congrArg Prod.fst h)
  cover p q := by
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨ha,hx⟩
      obtain ⟨i,hi⟩ := (F.cover _ _).mp ha
      exact ⟨i,Prod.ext hi (by simpa only [hi] using hx)⟩
    · rintro ⟨i,hi⟩
      have hv := congrArg Prod.fst hi
      exact ⟨(F.cover _ _).mpr ⟨i,hv⟩, by simpa only [← hv] using congrArg Prod.snd hi⟩

    if e.val.2 = v then scalar (inverseScalar (s e)) (c e) else 0
  map_zero' := by

      z := by

    · have hfv : f.val.2 ≠ e.val.2 := by

def outgoingSlope (s : OrientedEdge G → Fin 3) (u v : Fin m) : Fin 3 :=
  if h : u < v ∧ G.Adj u v then s ⟨(u,v),h⟩
  else if h : v < u ∧ G.Adj v u then inverseScalar (s ⟨(v,u),h⟩)

theorem outgoing_affine (s : OrientedEdge G → Fin 3) (c : OrientedEdge G → Four)
    (u v : Fin m) (x : Four) :

      (affineTransport G s c).map u v 0 := by
  by_cases h : u < v ∧ G.Adj u v
  · simp [affineTransport, outgoingSlope, orientedMap, h, affineThree, scalar_zero]
  · by_cases h' : v < u ∧ G.Adj v u
    · simp [affineTransport, outgoingSlope, orientedMap, h, h', affineThree, scalar_add, scalar_zero]
    · simp [affineTransport, outgoingSlope, orientedMap, h, h', scalar]

local predicate; constructing an orientation satisfying it remains separate. -/
def OmegaWalk (s : OrientedEdge G → Fin 3) {u v : Fin m} (p : G.Walk u v) : Prop := by
  induction p with
  | nil => exact True
  | @cons u v w _ _ ih => exact outgoingSlope G s u v = 1 ∧ ih

    ∃ b : Four, ∀ x, (affineTransport G s c).along p x = scalar (Fin.ofNat 3 p.length) x + b := by

  | nil => exact ⟨0,fun x => by simp [EdgeTransport.along, scalar]⟩
  | @cons u v w h p ih =>
    obtain ⟨b,hb⟩ := ih hp.2
    refine ⟨scalar (Fin.ofNat 3 p.length) ((affineTransport G s c).map u v 0) + b,fun x => ?_⟩
    change (affineTransport G s c).along p ((affineTransport G s c).map u v x) = _
    rw [hb, outgoing_affine, hp.1, scalar_add]
    have he : Fin.ofNat 3 (p.length+1) = Fin.ofNat 3 p.length + 1 := by
      apply Fin.ext
      simp [Fin.ofNat, Fin.add_def, Nat.add_mod]
    rw [SimpleGraph.Walk.length_cons, he, scalar_comp]
    simp only [add_assoc]

nonidentity affine holonomy, including the reversed scalar case. -/

    ∃ a b, ∀ x, (affineTransport G s c).along p x = affine a b x := by

    intro hh
    have hv := congrArg Fin.val hh

    have hv := (Fin.ofNat 3 p.length).isLt
    have hz : (Fin.ofNat 3 p.length).val ≠ 0 := fun h => he (Fin.ext h)
    rcases (by omega : (Fin.ofNat 3 p.length).val = 1 ∨ (Fin.ofNat 3 p.length).val = 2) with h | h
    · exact Or.inl (Fin.ext h)
    · exact Or.inr (Fin.ext h)
  rcases hc with h | h
  · exact ⟨true,b,fun x => by rw [hb,h,scalar_one]; rfl⟩
  · exact ⟨false,b,fun x => by rw [hb,h,scalar_two]; rfl⟩

  classical
  have hc : ∀ v, (T.fibre r v)ᶜ.card = 1 := by
    intro v
    rw [Finset.card_compl, hs v]

def incidenceD (s : OrientedEdge G → Fin 3) :
    (Fin m → Four) →+ (OrientedEdge G → Four) where
  toFun b e := b e.val.2 + scalar (s e) (b e.val.1)
  map_zero' := by funext e; simp only [Pi.zero_apply, scalar_zero, add_zero]
  map_add' b b' := by
    funext e
    simp only [Pi.add_apply, scalar_add]
    abel

    (c : OrientedEdge G → Four)

    c ∈ (incidenceD G s).range := by
  obtain ⟨b,hb⟩ := h

  funext e

  rw [forward_affine] at h
  have hh := congrArg (fun z => z + scalar (s e) (b e.val.1)) h

    simpa [add_assoc, add_comm, add_left_comm, four_add_self] using hh
  exact he.symm

    (c : OrientedEdge G → Four) (r : Fin m × Four)

  constants_in_range_of_section G s c ((affineTransport G s c).section_of_singleton r h)

    (c : OrientedEdge G → Four) (r : Fin m × Four)
    (h : ∀ v, ((affineTransport G s c).fibre r v).card = 3) :
    c ∈ (incidenceD G s).range :=
  constants_in_range_of_section G s c ((affineTransport G s c).section_of_three r h)

namespace XorMagic
abbrev Bits (n : ℕ) := Fin n → ZMod 2

variable {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]

def OpenMagic (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (n : ℕ) : Prop :=
  G.Connected ∧ ∃ l : V ≃ Bits n, ∀ v, ∑ u ∈ G.neighborFinset v, l u = 0

def ClosedMagic (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (n : ℕ) : Prop :=
  G.Connected ∧ ∃ l : V ≃ Bits n, ∀ v, l v + ∑ u ∈ G.neighborFinset v, l u = 0

theorem card_of_label {n : ℕ} (l : V ≃ Bits n) : Fintype.card V = 2^n := by
  simpa [Bits, Fintype.card_fun] using Fintype.card_congr l

def OpenExists (n d : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ (V : Type) (_ : Fintype V) (_ : DecidableEq V) (G : SimpleGraph V)
    (_ : DecidableRel G.Adj), G.IsRegularOfDegree d ∧ OpenMagic G n

def ClosedExists (n d : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ (V : Type) (_ : Fintype V) (_ : DecidableEq V) (G : SimpleGraph V)
    (_ : DecidableRel G.Adj), G.IsRegularOfDegree d ∧ ClosedMagic G n

def PrintedAt (n : ℕ) : Prop :=
  (∀ d, Odd d → 5 ≤ d → d ≤ 2^n-5 → OpenExists n d) ∧
  (∀ d, Even d → 4 ≤ d → d ≤ 2^n-4 → ClosedExists n d)

def CorrectedAt (n : ℕ) : Prop :=
  (∀ d, Odd d → 5 ≤ d → d ≤ 2^n-5 → OpenExists n d) ∧
  (∀ d, Even d → 4 ≤ d → d ≤ 2^n-6 → ClosedExists n d)

  ext i
  exact CharTwo.add_self_eq_zero (x i)

theorem cubic_obstruction {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (reg : G.IsRegularOfDegree 3) (l : V ≃ Bits n)

  let z := l.symm 0
  have hz : l z = 0 := l.apply_symm_apply 0
  have hc : (G.neighborFinset z).card = 3 := by simpa using reg z
  obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := Finset.card_pos.mp (by omega : 0 < (G.neighborFinset z).card)

    simpa only [SimpleGraph.mem_neighborFinset] using (show G.Adj z u from (by simpa using hu)).symm

    rw [Finset.card_erase_of_mem hzu]
    have : (G.neighborFinset u).card = 3 := by simpa using reg u

  have hs : ∑ x ∈ (G.neighborFinset u).erase z, l x = 0 := by
    have h := magic u
    rw [← Finset.sum_erase_add _ _ hzu, hz, add_zero] at h
    exact h

  have hs' : l a + l b = 0 := by simpa [hab] using hs
  have hequal : l a = l b := by
    have h := congrArg (fun x => x + l b) hs'
    simpa [add_assoc, bits_add_self] using h
  exact hab (l.injective hequal)

theorem complement_identity {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (l : V → Bits n) (total : ∑ v, l v = 0) (v : V) :
    (∑ u ∈ Gᶜ.neighborFinset v, l u) = l v + ∑ u ∈ G.neighborFinset v, l u := by

  have hn : v ∉ G.neighborFinset v := by simp
  have hd : Disjoint (G.neighborFinset v) (Gᶜ.neighborFinset v) := by
    apply Finset.disjoint_left.mpr
    intro u hu hc
    have ha : G.Adj v u := by simpa using hu
    have hb : Gᶜ.Adj v u := by simpa using hc
    exact hb.2 ha
  have hp : insert v (G.neighborFinset v ∪ Gᶜ.neighborFinset v) = Finset.univ := by
    ext u
    simp only [Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_union, SimpleGraph.mem_neighborFinset,
      SimpleGraph.compl_adj, Finset.mem_univ, iff_true]
    by_cases h : u = v

    · by_cases ha : G.Adj v u
      · exact Or.inr (Or.inl ha)

    (∑ w ∈ H.neighborFinset v, l (e.symm w)) = ∑ u ∈ G.neighborFinset (e.symm v), l u := by

  apply Finset.sum_bij (fun w _ => e.symm w)
  · intro w hw
    simpa only [SimpleGraph.mem_neighborFinset, ← e.symm.map_adj_iff] using hw
  · intro a _ b _ h
    exact e.symm.injective h
  · intro u hu
    refine ⟨e u, ?_, by simp⟩
    simpa only [SimpleGraph.mem_neighborFinset, ← e.map_adj_iff, RelIso.apply_symm_apply] using hu
  · intro w _; rfl

  intro w
  have hc := Fintype.card_congr (e.mapNeighborSet (e.symm w))
  have hh : H.degree w = G.degree (e.symm w) := by
    simpa only [RelIso.apply_symm_apply, SimpleGraph.card_neighborSet_eq_degree] using hc.symm
  exact hh.trans (h _)

theorem relabel_open (e : G ≃g H) (h : OpenMagic G n) : OpenMagic H n := by
  obtain ⟨hc,l,hl⟩ := h
  refine ⟨?_, e.symm.toEquiv.trans l, ?_⟩
  · exact hc.map e.toHom e.surjective
  · intro w
    exact (relabel_neighbor_sum e l w).trans (hl _)

theorem relabel_closed (e : G ≃g H) (h : ClosedMagic G n) : ClosedMagic H n := by
  obtain ⟨hc,l,hl⟩ := h
  refine ⟨?_, e.symm.toEquiv.trans l, ?_⟩
  · exact hc.map e.toHom e.surjective
  · intro w
    change l (e.symm w) + (∑ u ∈ H.neighborFinset w, l (e.symm u)) = 0
    rw [relabel_neighbor_sum]
    exact hl _

namespace XorMagic
variable {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]

/-- Fixed point free involutions partition all graph edges, with distinct mates at each vertex. -/
structure MatchingDecomposition (G : SimpleGraph V) (d : ℕ) where
  mate : Fin d → V → V
  involutive : ∀ i v, mate i (mate i v) = v
  no_fixed : ∀ i v, mate i v ≠ v
  distinct : ∀ v, Function.Injective (fun i => mate i v)
  cover : ∀ v w, G.Adj v w ↔ ∃ i, mate i v = w

structure FactorCycleData (G : SimpleGraph V) (d : ℕ) where
  factors : MatchingDecomposition G d
  complementFactors : MatchingDecomposition Gᶜ (Fintype.card V-1-d)
  two_le : 2 ≤ d
  length : ℕ
  positive : 0 < length
  not_three : length % 3 ≠ 0
  cycle : Fin length → V
  injective : Function.Injective cycle
  edges : ∀ i, factors.mate ⟨0, by omega⟩ (cycle i) = cycle ⟨(i.val+1)%length, Nat.mod_lt _ positive⟩ ∨
    factors.mate ⟨1, by omega⟩ (cycle i) = cycle ⟨(i.val+1)%length, Nat.mod_lt _ positive⟩

structure LiftSeed (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (n d : ℕ) (closed : Bool) where
  regular : G.IsRegularOfDegree d
  magic : if closed then ClosedMagic G n else OpenMagic G n
  factorCycle : FactorCycleData G d
end XorMagic

    (p : G.Walk (C.cycle ⟨0,C.positive⟩) (C.cycle ⟨0,C.positive⟩))

  intro i hi
  have hil : i < C.length := by omega
  rw [hind ⟨i,hil⟩]
  by_cases hs : i+1 < C.length
  · rw [hind ⟨i+1,hs⟩]
    simpa only [Nat.mod_eq_of_lt hs] using C.outgoing ⟨i,hil⟩
  · have he : i+1 = C.length := by omega
    have hp : p.getVert (i+1) = C.cycle ⟨0,C.positive⟩ := by
      simpa only [he, hlen] using p.getVert_length
    rw [hp]
    simpa only [he,Nat.mod_self] using C.outgoing ⟨i,hil⟩

    (hind : ∀ i : Fin C.length, p.getVert i.val = C.cycle i)
    (hstart : C.colouring.colour (C.cycle ⟨0,C.positive⟩) = true)
    (e : K ≃g G) : ColouredSeed G n d closed := by
  let D := C.relabel e
